subject: lost wallet
title: What If You Lost 17,000 Wallets on Purpose? Scientists Did

scenes.text: What if you lost 17,000 wallets on purpose? Scientists did, and the experts called it wrong.
Researchers handed in 17,303 wallets at banks, hotels, museums and police stations in 355 cities, saying they'd found them.
Each held a key, a grocery list and business cards with an email address. Some had no cash, some about 13 dollars.
Beforehand, 279 economists and experts made predictions. They expected cash to make people keep the wallet.
It went the other way. No money: 40 percent reported. With money: 51 percent. It held in 38 of 40 countries.
With about 94 dollars inside, it rose to 72 percent. The researchers' explanation: people can't stand feeling like a thief.

description:
What if you dropped thousands of wallets around the world to see who gave them back? For a 2019 study in Science, researchers turned in 17,303 wallets at front desks in 355 cities in 40 countries.
Wallets with no money were reported 40 percent of the time; wallets with about 13 dollars, 51 percent; and wallets with about 94 dollars, 72 percent. Wallets with money were more likely to be returned in 38 of the 40 countries. A panel of 279 economists and experts had predicted the opposite.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Denmark returned 82 percent of the wallets with money. What would your town score? What should we run through next?
